account: Today seems quiet from what I have personally seen and heard. I read my appointments, attended the morning market walk, bought a loaf, spent the noon lunch period at home, and have now returned to the town hall for the scheduled thirteen-hundred town accounts. Several residents I asked said they had no news. I asked freight about the docks and warehouse, but heard no reply, so I have no evidence of a problem there. The only unresolved matter I know of is my fifteen-hundred tea appointment: the book says only 'the neighbour, dockside cottage, east bank,' without a name or exact address. The secretary said she would visit the cottages to identify the host and confirm the location before fifteen hundred. I have not yet heard her findings. She also took the appointment book after I returned it so she could manage my schedule. I am now beside the treasury chest, but have not inspected its contents, so I cannot yet say anything about the town accounts. Nothing I have observed establishes unusual activity or a hidden purpose; the secretary's inquiries appear intended simply to ensure I reach the correct tea appointment.
